tables.name: tasks
rows: Walk the human through one task in Casefile, from start to finish

Tutorial task. The human has just installed Casefile and wants to see how an agent works in the tracker and what is left for them to do. You go through one real task together with them, step by step, and hand them a memo at the end.

The human watches the whole cycle of one task live and recognises their own part in it: you ask them a question and continue from their answer, take their remark and resolve it, and close the task. The result is a memo for the human that ends with the two moves that start their real work.

Environment.
- Casefile board: `http://localhost:8080`. This task's page: `http://localhost:8080/tasks/START-1`.
- The human is participant `owner`; address the question to them.
- The human answers a question in the "Inbox" section of the side panel or on the task page; they leave a remark with the "Leave a remark" form on the task page.
- You talk to the human in the chat — the one where you got this phrase.
- Everything you file shows up for the human on the board at once.

- Write case entries and the memo in the language of the human's message to you.
- No repository, files or network are needed: all the work happens in the tracker and the chat. Create no other tasks or projects.
- The question and the remark are the human's own steps: never answer your own question and never file the remark yourself.
- Keep chat messages short: one step, one message.

Build the case in this order — one numbered step, one action. Below, `key` (`task` for `wait_journal`) is always `START-1`.

1. `update_task` — `changes.assignee` your own name, for example `agent`.
2. `transition` — `to: in_progress`. Refused with `assignee_mismatch`? Take the name from the refusal's `details`, redo step 1 with it, then repeat this step.
3. In chat, say word for word: "Open `http://localhost:8080/tasks/START-1` — every step will show up there."
4. `ask` — `addressees: [owner]`, `blocking: true`, a `title` and `body` asking which piece of their own work the human would hand to an agent first.
5. `add_summary` — `done`, `remaining`, `blockers`, `next_step`: say you asked the question and are waiting for the answer.
6. `transition` — `to: waiting`, a `reason` naming the question you wait for.
7. In chat, say word for word: "Answer the question in the 'Inbox' section or on the task page. If after that I have stopped here and gone quiet, write me 'Answered'." Do not end your turn after this line: go straight to step 8.
8. `wait_journal` — `types: [answer]`, `after: 0`, `timeout: 60`; repeat the call until an entry comes back. If your client can watch in the background, a watcher on the answer may replace the call. The human wrote 'Answered'? Do this step again: the entry is already there.
9. `transition` — `to: in_progress`.
10. `add_entry` — `type: artifact`, a `title`, `refs: [START-1#<the answer's number>]`, and a `body` — the memo below, with the work from the answer, in the human's own words, in place of the one placeholder:

What you do in Casefile: you answer the agent's questions, leave remarks on tasks, create and run projects, read their case.

Your work — <the work from your answer, in your own words> — goes to agents through the tracker: in two moves, in two separate sessions; between moves the context is lost completely, and the second agent knows only what is in the tracker.

Move one — describe this work to an agent and say: «File tasks in Casefile for my work: a project for it if there is none yet, and tasks with all their sections and checks, each small enough for one agent to finish in one go, each naming its environment in `context` — where the work lives and how to run its checks. Don't start the work itself; if I haven't described it yet, ask me.»
Move two — in a new agent session, say: «Carry out the tasks for this work from the Casefile tracker. Hand them to agents, one task per agent, to save your own context, and give them cheaper models where those cope.»

11. `add_summary` — `done`, `remaining`, `blockers`, `next_step`: say the memo is filed and you are waiting for a remark.
12. `transition` — `to: waiting`, a `reason` naming that you wait for a remark.
13. In chat, say word for word: "Leave any remark on the task with the 'Leave a remark' form on its page. If after that I have stopped here and gone quiet, write me 'Remark left'." Do not end your turn after this line: go straight to step 14.
14. `wait_journal` — `types: [remark]`, `after: 0`, `timeout: 60`; repeat the call until an entry comes back. If your client can watch in the background, a watcher on the remark may replace the call. The human wrote 'Remark left'? Do this step again: the entry is already there.
15. `transition` — `to: in_progress`.
16. `add_entry` — `type: artifact`, a `title`, `refs: [START-1#<the memo's number>]`, and a `body` — the same memo with only what the remark asked for changed; both move lines stay word for word.
17. `resolve` — the `remark_no` of the remark, `outcome: fixed`, naming what changed in `body`.
18. `close_task` — a `verdicts` entry for every check and a closing `summary`.
19. In chat, say word for word: "The tour is over: project START can be archived from its page, and real work starts with the two moves from the memo."

["The case holds a question to the human participant and their `answer`.", "The `answer` and the `remark` were both filed while the task stood in `waiting` with a reason, and after each the task came back to `in_progress`.", "The `remark` has an outcome through `resolve`; the corrected memo is filed as an `artifact` before it.", "An `artifact` with the memo is filed after the answer, and its `refs` name the answer's entry."]
